headline: Southborough advanced a $38 million Neary School addition-renovation design, approved key Special Town Meeting funding articles, and initiated FY28 override budget planning.
synopsis: In October 2026, the Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance a $38 million addition-renovation plan for Neary School to schematic design after learning a basic $15 million upgrade would fund minimal repairs. At Special Town Meeting, voters approved Community Preservation Act funding for both the Peninsula Trail footbridge and the Southborough Golf Club irrigation overhaul, but rejected a two-family zoning amendment after an 85-80 vote fell short of a two-thirds majority. Municipal boards ramped up FY28 budget preparations under tight fiscal conditions, modeling both level-service requests and level-funded scenarios that would trigger operational cutbacks if a Proposition 2 1/2 override fails. The Regional School Committee re-voted its FY27 budget downward following increased Chapter 70 state aid and highlighted an anticipated $800,000 drop in regional debt service heading into FY28. Meanwhile, the Planning Board approved site plan modifications on Turnpike Road and extended its decision deadline on the proposed Route 9 Costco development into December.

top_items.title: Neary School addition-renovation plan advances to schematic design
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted unanimously to proceed with a $38 million addition-renovation after architects showed a $15 million option left just $5.8 million for direct construction.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects reported that after deducting code-mandated sprinkler systems, accessibility requirements, and soft costs, a $15 million upgrade would not fund boiler replacements, mechanical systems, or educational improvements. The committee voted 4-0 on October 21 to advance Option 3 for detailed schematic design, cost breakdowns, and site modeling ahead of an anticipated spring 2027 Town Meeting vote.

top_items.title: Special Town Meeting approves Peninsula Trail footbridge CPA funding
top_items.why: Voters approved up to $428,550 in Community Preservation Act funds to build a pedestrian footbridge connecting trail segments.
top_items.body: After the Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to keep the warrant article intact without proposed funding reductions, the Trails Committee dropped a fallback floor amendment and presented the full request. Town Meeting approved Article 4, allowing the committee to move into planning safe road crossings with DPW and MassDOT and pursuing state grant matches.

top_items.title: Town boards begin FY28 budget reviews facing potential override
top_items.why: Town officials are preparing FY28 spending plans around level-service needs or level-funded cuts to address a projected operating deficit exceeding $2 million.
top_items.body: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee began reviewing $2.15 million in capital appropriation requests and up to $49 million in bondable projects, heavily driven by school infrastructure. Meanwhile, town departments drafted dual budget scenarios, with the Board of Health detailing reduced inspection hours and Friday office closures if a municipal override fails.

top_items.title: Regional school district outlines $800,000 debt drop and revised budget
top_items.why: Expiration of original high school renovation debt will lower regional debt service by $800,000 in FY28, while increased state aid lowered FY27 town assessments.
top_items.body: School budget subcommittees learned that retiring 2004 high school debt will yield an $800,000 net reduction in FY28 debt service even after accounting for the new athletic complex. On October 29, the Regional School Committee re-voted a revised $31.52 million FY27 budget to incorporate $104,890 in additional state Chapter 70 aid, slightly reducing Southborough's assessment to $10.73 million.

top_items.title: Planning Board extends Costco review deadline to December
top_items.why: The Planning Board continued public hearings on the 167,000-square-foot Costco proposal and extended its statutory decision deadline to December 18, 2026.
top_items.body: Awaiting completed consultant peer review studies on traffic impacts along Route 9, the Planning Board voted 5-0 to continue hearings on the Costco major site plan and special permits to a special November 2 meeting. The board also extended its statutory deadline to issue a final decision to December 18.

top_items.title: Town Meeting rejects two-family zoning while senior housing bylaw progresses
top_items.why: A two-family zoning amendment failed at Town Meeting by falling short of a two-thirds majority, prompting boards to pivot toward 55-plus housing updates.
top_items.body: Article 2 failed to pass Special Town Meeting despite an 85-80 majority vote, leading the Zoning Board of Appeals to pause local changes and await pending state legislation. Meanwhile, the Affordable Housing Trust reached consensus to advance a revised 55-plus zoning bylaw that removes Southborough's 7 percent cap on age-restricted housing while setting a two-acre minimum lot size and an eight-unit-per-acre density ceiling.

top_items.title: Special Town Meeting approves funding for golf course irrigation overhaul
top_items.why: Town Meeting approved Article 3, authorizing $433,546 in CPA funds and $100,000 from the Golf Revolving Fund to overhaul the course irrigation system.
top_items.body: Following outreach by the Golf Committee and support from the Community Preservation Committee, voters approved the required funding package to complete the $1.09 million replacement project. The Golf Committee also voted to contribute up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to cover a consultant shortfall for Audubon International certification, a condition of the project.
